cards.label: Muses
cards.general: Goddesses of song and poetry, daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne.
cards.here: They travel through the night singing the gods’ names.

cards.label: Eos
cards.general: Dawn imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is named alongside the Sun and Moon.

cards.label: Helios
cards.general: The Sun imagined as a god.
cards.here: Hesiod calls him great.

cards.label: Selene
cards.general: The Moon imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is described as bright.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: The Earth imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is included among the eternal gods.

cards.label: Night
cards.general: Night imagined as a goddess, called Nyx in Greek.
cards.here: She is described as black.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: The Earth imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She and Uranus are parents of an early generation of gods.

cards.label: Uranus
cards.general: The Sky imagined as a god.
cards.here: With Gaia, he fathers the gods whose family history the Muses sing.

evidence.reason: Earth is the translated name of the divine mother.
Sky is the translated name of the divine father.

cards.label: Himeros
cards.general: The god who represents desire and longing.
cards.here: He lives near the Muses and the Graces.

evidence.reason: Desire translates Himeros’s name.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: Earth herself, understood as a goddess.
cards.here: An ancestor of the gods.

cards.label: Uranus
cards.general: The Sky, understood as a god.
cards.here: The starry Sky from whom gods were born.

cards.label: Pontus
cards.general: The Sea, understood as a god.
cards.here: He brings up some of the gods.

cards.label: Chaos
cards.general: Chaos is the primordial gap that first comes into being.
cards.here: Erebus and Night are born from Chaos. The name means a gap or chasm.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: Earth herself, imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: Her broad body provides a firm seat for everything.

cards.label: Tartarus
cards.general: Tartarus is the primordial depth, a dark region beneath earth.
cards.here: It appears among the earliest entities to come into being.

cards.label: Eros
cards.general: The divine power of love and sexual desire.
cards.here: His power weakens limbs and overwhelms clear thinking in gods and humans alike.

cards.label: Erebus
cards.general: Darkness imagined as a divine being.
cards.here: He comes from Chaos and fathers Aether and Day with Night.

cards.label: Aether
cards.general: Aether is the divine bright upper air, a child of Night and Erebus.
cards.here: He is born alongside Day after his parents join in love.

cards.general: Gaia is the primordial goddess Earth.
cards.here: She bears Sky, the Mountains, and Pontus without a partner, then bears the Titans with Sky.

cards.label: Mountains
cards.general: The Mountains are primordial offspring of Gaia.
cards.here: They are born as homes for the mountain Nymphs; no individual mountains are named.

cards.label: Uranus
cards.general: Sky himself, imagined as a god.
cards.here: Earth bears him and later has children with him.

cards.label: Pontus
cards.general: The Sea itself, imagined as a god.
cards.here: Earth gives birth to him without a partner.

cards.general: Gaia is the goddess Earth, and Uranus is the god Sky.
cards.here: They are the parents of the Cyclopes and the three Hundred-Handers described here.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: Cronus is a Titan son of Gaia and Uranus.
cards.here: He cuts off his father’s genitals and throws them into the sea, continuing the action of the preceding passage.

cards.label: Aphrodite
cards.general: The goddess of love, sexual attraction, and pleasure.
cards.here: She grows in sea foam and steps ashore on Cyprus.

cards.label: Eros
cards.general: Love, especially sexual attraction, imagined as a god.
cards.here: He accompanies Aphrodite from her birth.

cards.general: Longing or desire, imagined as a god.

cards.general: Uranus is the primordial god Sky, father of the Titans by Gaia.
cards.here: He rebukes his children and connects their name with their deed and the punishment to come.

cards.label: Moros
cards.general: Doom or an unavoidable fate, imagined as a divine being.
cards.here: He is Night’s first child named in this list.

cards.label: Thanatos
cards.general: Death himself, imagined as a god.
cards.here: He is a child of Night and a brother of Sleep.

cards.label: Hypnos
cards.general: Sleep himself, imagined as a god.

cards.label: Momus
cards.general: Blame or fault-finding, imagined as a god.
cards.here: He is one of Night’s children.

cards.label: Oizys
cards.general: Misery or distress, imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: Hesiod describes her as painful.

cards.label: Nemesis
cards.general: A goddess of resentment and deserved payback for wrongdoing.
cards.here: Night bears her as a source of suffering for mortals.

cards.label: Apate
cards.general: Deceit imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is born after Nemesis.

cards.label: Philotes
cards.general: Affection or intimacy, including sexual intimacy, imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is another child of Night.

cards.label: Eris
cards.general: Strife or conflict imagined as a goddess.
cards.here: She is Night’s fierce-hearted child.

cards.label: Quarrels
cards.general: The Neikea are divine personifications of quarrels, children of Strife.
cards.here: They are named with lying Words and Arguments.

cards.label: Arguments
cards.general: The Amphillogiai are divine personifications of arguments or disputes, children of Strife.

cards.label: Lawlessness
cards.general: Dysnomia is Strife’s divine personification of lawlessness.
cards.here: She and Ruin are close companions.

cards.label: Ruin
cards.general: Ate is Strife’s divine personification of ruin or disastrous blindness.
cards.here: She stays close to Lawlessness. Recklessness explains this destructive blindness; it is not another child.

cards.label: Oath
cards.general: Horkos is Strife’s divine child who punishes deliberate false swearing.

cards.label: Graiae
cards.general: The Graiae are Ceto and Phorcys’s supernatural daughters Pemphredo and Enyo, gray-haired from birth.
cards.here: Their name means Old Women, which Hesiod explains through their hair.

cards.label: Chrysaor
cards.general: Chrysaor is Medusa and Poseidon’s son, who emerges holding a golden sword.
cards.here: He springs out when Perseus cuts off Medusa’s head. His sword explains his name.

cards.label: Poseidon
cards.general: The god of the sea, often called “the Dark-haired One.”

cards.here: His union with Oceanus’s daughter produces three-headed Geryon.

cards.label: Athena

cards.here: Her guidance helps Heracles defeat the Hydra.

cards.label: Tethys
cards.general: Tethys is a Titan goddess, mother of the Oceanids and river gods by Ocean.
cards.here: She bears the daughters and Rivers who help nurture the young.

cards.label: Ocean
cards.general: Ocean is Oceanus, the world-encircling river god.
cards.here: He and Tethys are the parents of the Oceanid daughters and the Rivers.

cards.label: Rivers
cards.general: The Rivers are the river-god sons of Ocean and Tethys.
cards.here: They help Apollo and their sisters nurture the young, and number three thousand.

cards.label: Peitho
cards.general: Peitho is an Oceanid goddess who personifies persuasion.
cards.here: She is named among Ocean and Tethys’s eldest daughters.

cards.label: Dione
cards.general: Dione is an Oceanid goddess, a daughter of Ocean and Tethys.
cards.here: She is named among their eldest daughters and called lovely.

cards.label: Phoe

cards.here: One of the eldest daughters.

cards.label: Calypso
cards.general: Calypso is an Oceanid goddess, a daughter of Ocean and Tethys.
cards.here: She is named among their eldest daughters and called enchanting.

cards.label: Eosphorus
cards.general: Eosphorus is the divine Morning Star, a child of Eos and Astraeus.
cards.here: Eos bears him after the Winds. He is Venus as seen before sunrise.

cards.label: gleaming stars

cards.here: Eos bears them after the Winds, and they crown the sky.

cards.label: Zelos

cards.label: Kratos

cards.label: Cronus

cards.here: His name identifies Zeus through the title son of Cronus.

cards.label: Earth-shaker

cards.label: Zeus’s father’s brothers

evidence.reason: Links the actual translated phrase to the existing Cyclopes explanation, preserving its prose.

cards.label: The Seasons
cards.general: The Horae: goddesses who oversee the seasons and orderly life.
cards.here: Eunomia means Good Order, Dike means Justice, and Eirene means Peace. They watch over human work.

cards.label: The Fates
cards.general: Goddesses who determine people's allotted lives.
cards.here: Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos give people their share of good and bad. Their names suggest spinning, allotting, and what cannot be turned back.

cards.label: The Graces
